Retrieve historical forecast data at specific lead times

Source: R/get_historical_forecast.R
get_historical_forecast.Rd

Pulls archived GFS/NWS forecast model output from the Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API for a given location, date range, and set of forecast lead times. Returns the forecast that would have been issued lead_days before the valid date — i.e. what a model would have received as input on that day.

Usage

get_historical_forecast(
  lat = 44.390278,
  lon = -121.406792,
  start_date,
  end_date,
  lead_days = c(1, 3, 7),
  variables = c("temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min", "cloud_cover_mean"),
  model = "gfs_seamless",
  timezone = "UTC"
)

Arguments

lat

Numeric. Latitude of target point.

lon

Numeric. Longitude of target point.

start_date

Character or Date. Start of valid date range.

end_date

Character or Date. End of valid date range.

lead_days

Integer vector. Forecast lead times in days. e.g. c(1, 3, 7) returns the day-1, day-3, and day-7 forecasts.

variables

Character vector. Daily forecast variables to retrieve.

model

Character. Forecast model to use. "gfs_seamless" is the closest to NWS operational output. Other options: "ecmwf_ifs04", "gfs025", "icon_seamless".

timezone

Character. Timezone. Defaults to "UTC".

Value

A tibble with columns: valid_date, issue_date, lead_days, variable, value, units, lat, lon

Details

The Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API archives GFS model runs from 2020 onwards at daily resolution. The forecast_days parameter controls how many days ahead each archived run extends. By requesting the same valid date from runs issued at different lead times, you can reconstruct what the forecast said at each lead time.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
get_historical_forecast(
  lat        = 44.390278,
  lon        = -121.406792,
  start_date = "2023-07-01",
  end_date   = "2023-07-31",
  lead_days  = c(1, 3, 7)
)
} # }
